Rawshan Ali Sarker (Md) ------ Petitioner

Bangladesh and  others --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Dhaka Bank Ltd. being plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No. 267 of 2015 to the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura for recovery of out-standing loan to the tune of Taka 4,04,85,429.79. Having received the summons of the said suit, the petitioner entered appearance in the Suit. Eventually, the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura, hereinafter shortly referred to 'the Adalat', was pleased to decree the Suit as prayed for. Thereafter, the decree-holder put the decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No. 165 of 2017, hereinafter shortly called as 'the Execution Case'. 

 3. In Execution Case, the judgment-debtor filed an application on 9-4-2018 (Annexure-E) to give him installment for a period of 3 (three) years for payment of Taka 2,32,00,000 (two crore thirty two lac). On the same date, the decree-holder also filed another application (Annexure-E1) to hold settlement conference in view of section 45 of the Ain, 2003. The decree-holder filed an application for publishing notice in the daily newspaper to sell out the mortgage property on auction. 

 4. Upon hearing, the Executing Court allowed the petition of the decree-holder and rejected the applications of the judgment-debtor on 9-4-2018 and accordingly, 26-4-2018 was fixed for taking step for publishing auction notice. By its order dated 10-6-2018, the Executing Court directed to float notice in the daily newspapers fixing 5-7-2018 for auction sale of the mortgage property. 

 6. Mr Md Aktaruzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the Executing Court most illegally and arbitrarily rejected the petition filed under section 49 of the Ain, 2003 for installment without assigning any good reasons and, therefore, the same is liable to be turned down by this Court. He further submits that the Adalat, without giving the opportunity to the judgment-debtor and decree-holder to exhaust the provision of section 45 of the Ain, 2003 to resolve the dispute by way of mediation, most illegally rejected the prayer for settlement conference which is illegal. 

 8. He also submits that section 6(2) of the Ain, 2003 makes it abundantly clear that the requirements laid down in the section are mandatory and not obligatory in nature. The language using this section makes it clear that the plaint has to be filed along with an affidavit both as to the statement made in the plaint as well as to the document annexed to the plaint, therefore, the non compliance with the mandatory requirement of law rendered in the plaint rejected in the eye of law and consequently, the decree passed by the Adalat cannot sustain in the eye of law. 

 10. Mr AM Amin Uddin further submits that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree, save few exceptions. He further submits that the application prayed for time to pay the decretal amount by installment was rightly rejected by the impugned order No. 10, dated 9-4-2018 and in the meantime, 2 years have already been elapsed but the petitioner did not pay single farthing nor contacted with the respondent Bank which amply implies that the judgment-debtor has no bonafide intention to pay off the outstanding decretal amount. 

 11. He further submits that in order to prolong the execution case, the petitioner filed this writ petition as a device so that the decree-holder cannot enjoy the fruits of the long cherished decree. He further submits that the petitioner has not come with clean hands. He further submits that the petitioner has got no bonafide intention to pay the outstanding dues. Finally, he submits that without preferring appeal to the competent Court, the chastity or legality of the decree of the Adalat cannot be challenged by invoking writ jurisdiction, therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 15. It also appears from the record (Annexure-I) that the petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 88 of 2018 to the Court of District Judge, Bogura challenging the decree of the Adalat. After that, the learned District Judge called for the record. Upon considering the materials on record, the learned District Judge by its order dated 23-5-2018 rejected the appeal summarily as it has got no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal. But the decree-holder did not challenge the said order nor file any appeal to the competent Court having jurisdiction to entertain the appeal in view of section 41 of the Ain, 2003. 

 20. It is well settled principle of Apex Court that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree, save few exceptions; if it appears to the executing court that the decree is nullity in the eye of law or the decree is passed against dead man or decree is passed by the court having no jurisdiction. 

 25. At the time of pronouncement of the judgment, the learned Advocate of the petitioner orally apprises that he has instruction by his client not to proceed with the case. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and to prevent multiplicity of proceeding on self-same cause, we hold the view that it would be advisable to dispose of the Rule on merit. Moreover, the backdrop of the case, palpably indicates the petitioner in order to frustrate the hard-earned decree has taken different devices. We do not find any substance therein and hence, we have disposed of the Rule on merit. 

 27. In appears from the record, the Artha Rin Suit and then Execution Case has been dragging for about 5 years. The main purpose of the Ain, 2003 is to dispense speedy justice but our experience shows that the borrower takes many devices to prolong the execution proceeding so that the decree holder cannot enjoy the fruits of decree. If the Execution Case is not disposed of within a reasonable time, the purpose of promulgating the Ain, 2003 will be frustrated. Therefore, the Executing Court is hereby directed to dispose of the Execution Case preferably within 06 (six) months from the date of receiving the copy of the judgment and no adjournment will be allowed from either side.
